# BeautifulRust drop-in lints
#
# Paste this into your Cargo.toml (or replace [lints] with [workspace.lints] in a
# workspace root and add `[lints] workspace = true` to each member). It makes clippy
# enforce the rules from the rust-best-practices skill that a machine can check.
# Everything is "warn"; make CI strict with:
#
#     cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
#
# Silence a lint locally with a reason, which the config below requires:
#
#     #[expect(clippy::unwrap_used, reason = "the regex is a literal and always compiles")]
#
# Lints marked [lib] fit libraries; applications can drop them.

[lints.rust]
unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "warn"          # each unsafe op needs its own unsafe block
missing_debug_implementations = "warn"   # every public type implements Debug
missing_docs = "warn"                    # [lib] document every public item
unreachable_pub = "warn"                 # pub items that aren't actually exported
rust_2018_idioms = { level = "warn", priority = -1 } # 2018-edition idioms, e.g. Formatter<'_>

[lints.clippy]
# Groups first, at lower priority so the individual settings below win.
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

# Panics: return errors, and give every intentional panic a reason.
unwrap_used = "warn"                     # use ?, or expect("why this cannot fail")
expect_used = "allow"                    # expect with a reason is the sanctioned form
panic_in_result_fn = "warn"              # a fn returning Result shouldn't also panic
missing_panics_doc = "warn"              # [lib] document reachable panics under # Panics
missing_errors_doc = "warn"              # [lib] document failures under # Errors
missing_assert_message = "warn"          # assert! says what went wrong (quiet inside #[test])

# Suppressions must explain themselves and expire when no longer needed.
allow_attributes = "warn"                # prefer #[expect] over #[allow] (needs rust-version 1.81+)
allow_attributes_without_reason = "warn" # every suppression says why (needs rust-version 1.81+)

# Unsafe must be justified.
undocumented_unsafe_blocks = "warn"      # // SAFETY: comment on every unsafe block
multiple_unsafe_ops_per_block = "warn"   # one unsafe operation per block

# API shape.
fn_params_excessive_bools = "warn"       # bool parameters: use an enum or two methods
struct_excessive_bools = "warn"          # many bool fields: use an enum or bitflags
clone_on_ref_ptr = "warn"                # write Rc::clone(&x) so cheap clones are visible
redundant_clone = "warn"                 # a clone whose original is never used again
rc_buffer = "warn"                       # Rc<String> / Rc<Vec<T>>: use Rc<str> / Rc<[T]>

# Evolution.
exhaustive_enums = "warn"                # [lib] exported enums are #[non_exhaustive] (quiet in binaries)

# Idioms.
string_add = "warn"                      # build strings with format! or push_str, not +
wildcard_imports = "warn"                # no glob imports (use super::* in tests is allowed)

# Output and debugging leftovers.
dbg_macro = "warn"
todo = "warn"
print_stdout = "warn"                    # [lib] libraries log, they don't print
print_stderr = "warn"                    # [lib] libraries log, they don't print

# Casts that silently lose information.
as_conversions = "warn"                  # prefer From / TryFrom
cast_possible_truncation = "warn"
cast_sign_loss = "warn"

# Pedantic lints that are mostly noise in practice, or that the skill disagrees with.
module_name_repetitions = "allow"
must_use_candidate = "allow"
module_inception = "allow"               # a leaf module named after its main item is fine
enum_glob_use = "allow"                  # use Enum::* inside a function that matches on it

Let me draft each finding precisely.

**Must fix 1 — the module does not compile** (`config.rs:6`, call site `config.rs:18`)
Rule: parameters take the widest borrow — `&str` not `&String` (`clippy::ptr_arg`; Rust API Guidelines borrowing guidance).
Problem: `parse_line` takes `&String`, but `load` passes `&str` from `text.lines()`. Deref coercion only goes `&String → &str`, never the reverse, so the crate fails with E0308 at the call site. Sharp observation: if `cargo check` currently passes on their tree, this file is not part of the build — check whether `mod config;` is even declared. Either way it breaks the moment it's wired in.
Fix: one-line signature change.

**Must fix 2 — `load` panics on the most ordinary config files** (`config.rs:18`)
Rule: no panics on reachable paths from external input — return an error (`M-PANIC-ON-BUG`, Microsoft Rust Guidelines).
Problem: `unwrap` on `parse_line`, whose `Err` case is *expected* (a line without `=`). `"a=1\n\n"` → `lines()` yields `["a=1", ""]`, blank line has no `=` → `Err("bad line: ")` → panic. Comments (`# ...`) same. Real config files have blank lines and comments; and in a library the panic fires in the caller's process.
Fix: `load` returns `Result`, `?` with line number (code). Needs finding 3's error type.

**Must fix 3 — `String` as the public error type** (`config.rs:6`)
Rule: C-GOOD-ERR (Rust API Guidelines) — errors implement `Display` + `std::error::Error`, callers match on variants.
Problem: `String` implements neither; callers can't match programmatically, and once published, changing the error type is a breaking change. Also the message has the offending line but no line number — the only caller that knows it is `load`.
Fix: enum with Display + Error + #[non_exhaustive].

**Should fix 4 — `splitn` + collect + len + index instead of `split_once`** (`config.rs:7-11`)
Rule: prefer the purpose-built stdlib API / combinator over check-then-index (idiom).
Problem: collect into a Vec, test `len() != 2`, then index — five lines for what `str::split_once` (stable since 1.52) expresses in one, without indexing.
Fix code.

**Should fix 5 — no tests** (whole file)
Rule: logic has no tests (skill's documentation-and-tests rule).
Problem: a single test with a blank line would have caught finding 2; no test compiles for finding 1. And there are no doc examples.
Fix: tests (short).

**Consider:**
6. `parse_line` is `pub` (`config.rs:6`) — the module doc promises loading, not line-parsing; making it public doubles API surface (and error surface). Make it private / `pub(crate)`.
7. Duplicate keys silently last-wins (`config.rs:19`) — fine as a convention but document it (`map.insert` overwrites). Or return an error.
8. Scope: no comment or blank-line support — defensible for a "simple" format, but say so in the module docs; currently a comment line is not "skipped", it's a panic (finding 2). After fixing, decide skip vs error.
9. `load` (`config.rs:15`) reads like disk I/O but takes in-memory text — rename to `parse`, or add a `Config` newtype with `FromStr`.

**What's already good:**
- `splitn(2, '=')` preserves `=` inside values (`k=a=b` → value `a=b`) — correct and easy to get wrong.
- Both key and value are trimmed.
- `load` takes `&str` — right borrow.
- The leaf uses `Result` rather than panicking or returning `Option` — the instinct is right; only the caller drops it.
- Both functions have doc comments.

- `missing_panics_doc` — even if kept, `load`'s panic would have to be documented as public API.
- `clippy::ptr_arg` (via the `all` group) — finding 1.

Also `exhaustive_enums` would nudge `#[non_exhaustive]` on ConfigError, `missing_errors_doc` would demand the `# Errors` doc on `load`. Nice — mention briefly.

Intro paragraph must state: library (user said library crate), verdict, single most important fix, and tools: clippy/fmt/test were NOT run — no Rust toolchain available in this environment (commands gated); review is by reading; both must-fix conclusions are compiler-semantics facts. Coercion rules: deref coercion `&String → &str` applies when expected type is `&str` and found is `&String` (String: Deref<Target=str>). For expected `&String` and found `&str`: there is no unsizing/deref path from `str` to `String` — `String` doesn't implement `Deref<Target=String>` from `str`, and unsized coercions go unsized→? actually unsizing coercion `&String → &str`... wait, technically `&String → &str` is a deref coercion; `&str → &String` would require `str → String` which is not an unsize coercion (String is Sized, target of unsize coercion must be unsized — so coercion direction is sized→unsized: `&String → &str` fits that: String sized, str unsized). `&str → &String` is unsized→sized, impossible. Confirmed: E0308.

And splitn semantics: `"abc".splitn(2, '=')` — iterator yields "abc" (one item). collect → Vec of len 1 → Err branch. Confirmed.

`"".lines()` yields nothing; `"a=1\n\n".lines()` yields "a=1", "" — confirmed (lines splits on \n, and an empty final segment after trailing newline is NOT yielded, but an interior blank line IS). `"a=1\n\n"` = "a=1" + "" + trailing newline → lines: ["a=1", ""]. Yes.

Panic message: `called \`Result::unwrap()\` on an \`Err\` value: "bad line: "` — the Err is a String with the line content (empty). Confirmed.

`str::split_once`: `pub fn split_once(&self, delimiter: char) -> Option<(&str, &str)>` — splits at first occurrence; for `"a=b=c"` → ("a", "b=c") — matches splitn(2) behavior exactly. Confirmed equivalent.

Display impl: `write!(f, "line {}: expected \`key=value\`, got \`{}\`", line, content)` — fine.

`#[non_exhaustive]` enum constructed within defining crate — allowed. Fine.

`ok_or_else` on Option<(String, String)> with closure returning ConfigError → Result<(String,String), ConfigError>; `?` works since ConfigError: no From needed (same error type). Fine.

One nit in my fix: `#[derive(Debug)]` on ConfigError — needed for `Error` impl? `std::error::Error` requires Debug + Display. Yes, Debug derive needed. Good, included.

Also in finding 5's tests, `assert!(err.to_string().contains("line 2"))` etc. — keep tests brief in the report; show 2-3.
